summary.prose: Building this Story adds dependency-advisory collection to the security-review module: a shared content-identity hash reused from s3, a manager-closure coverage check run both before and after each manager's audit, and a lockfile-export step that keeps an excluded private dependency excluded even through pip-audit's own resolution. The existing pkg_audit tool gains two small, additive fields; everything else (enumerating managers, computing the identity, checking closures, exporting lockfiles, and the orchestrator that ties them together) is new.

tasks.title: Add requirementsPath + noDeps fields to pkgAuditTool's inputSchema and auditArgv
tasks.summary: Add two optional inputSchema fields to pkgAuditTool (src/daemon/tools/builtins/pkg/index.ts): requirementsPath?: string and noDeps?: boolean. auditArgv gains the same two parameters: appends `-r <requirementsPath>` for pip/pipenv/poetry when provided, and `--no-deps` when noDeps is true. Both additive; omitted, every existing caller's behavior and argv is byte-for-byte unchanged.
acceptanceChecks: auditArgv('pip', {requirementsPath:'/tmp/x.txt'}) includes '-r /tmp/x.txt' in argv
auditArgv('pip', {noDeps:true}) includes '--no-deps' in argv
auditArgv('npm') with no new params produces the identical argv as today (no requirementsPath/noDeps leakage into unrelated managers)
pkgAuditTool's inputSchema declares both new fields as optional

tests.name: pkgAuditTool.execute: noDeps:true -> argv includes --no-deps
pkgAuditTool.execute: noDeps omitted/false -> argv is identical to today
auditArgv('pip', {requirementsPath}) appends -r <requirementsPath>
auditArgv('npm') with no new params is unchanged from today

tasks.title: Implement enumerateManagers
tasks.summary: enumerateManagers(repoPath, targets) walks repoPath to find every manager's manifest/lockfile, returning each detected manager with its manifestDir, and flags an unresolved ambiguity when two manifests for the same manager family appear in one directory.

two manifests for the same manager family in one directory are recorded as an unresolved ambiguity, never silently resolved to one
a directory with no recognizable manifest yields no manager for that directory

tasks.title: Implement computeContentIdentity
tasks.summary: computeContentIdentity(repoPath, targets) returns a deterministic digest over the repo's HEAD commit sha plus a sha256 of every file named in targets.entries' actual, current raw bytes -- a simple, shared, non-manager-aware hash (the same function s3 will also call over the same targets).
acceptanceChecks: editing an application-source file listed in targets.entries changes the digest
editing a file NOT in targets.entries leaves the digest unchanged
two calls with no intervening change to targets.entries' files yield the identical string
a targets.entries path resolving outside repoPath throws
repoPath that is not a registered git repository, or whose HEAD cannot be resolved, throws

computeContentIdentity: a file NOT in targets.entries is edited -> no change

tasks.title: Implement verifyManagerClosureCoverage
tasks.summary: verifyManagerClosureCoverage(repoPath, targets, manager, manifestDir) re-resolves a manager's required-input closure (nested -r/-c references for pip-family; a go module's full source tree for go) fresh on every call, and returns covered:true or covered:false with the missing files listed. Never caches a prior result.
acceptanceChecks: a manager's closure fully contained in targets.entries -> covered:true
a manager's closure referencing a file outside targets.entries -> covered:false with that file listed in missing
two calls in a row after a new file is added to the closure return different results (no caching)
never mutates targets.entries or any other input

tests.name: verifyManagerClosureCoverage: re-resolves the closure fresh on each call -- two calls in a row after a file is added return different results
verifyManagerClosureCoverage: a closure fully contained in targets.entries -> covered:true
verifyManagerClosureCoverage: a closure referencing a file outside targets.entries -> covered:false with missing listed

tasks.title: Implement lockfile export (requirementsPath generation) with faithful-export and version-uncertain gap detection
tasks.summary: For pipenv/poetry, generate a requirementsPath from Pipfile.lock/poetry.lock containing only plain-PyPI-sourced, faithfully-representable entries; a git/path/url-sourced or unfaithfully-representable entry is excluded and recorded as a non-standard-source gap (added to unresolvedDependencies). For plain pip, use the project's own requirements.txt directly; an entry that is not an exact pin is recorded as version-uncertain (also added to unresolvedDependencies), but the file itself is never rewritten. Every requirementsPath this step generates itself (pipenv/poetry only, never plain pip) is always paired with noDeps:true when later passed to pkgAuditTool (t1's fields).
acceptanceChecks: a poetry.lock entry with a git/path/url source is excluded from the generated file and recorded in unresolvedDependencies with a non-standard-source note
a poetry.lock entry with a plain PyPI source and exact version is included in the generated file (confirming the exact-locked version is preferred over a fresh resolution)
a plain pip requirements.txt entry using a version range (not an exact pin) is recorded in unresolvedDependencies as version-uncertain, while requirements.txt itself is left untouched
the generation step itself never sets noDeps -- that pairing happens at the collectDependencyAdvisories call site (t6)

tests.name: a poetry.lock entry with a git/path/url source -> excluded, added to unresolvedDependencies
a plain pip requirements.txt entry with a version range -> recorded in unresolvedDependencies as version-uncertain
a poetry.lock entry with an exact PyPI pin is included in the generated requirementsPath

tasks.title: Implement collectDependencyAdvisories
tasks.summary: collectDependencyAdvisories(repoPath, targets) orchestrates the full sc2 collection: computes contentIdentity once before any manager runs (propagating a failure here) and once after the last manager's audit completes (catching a failure here as contentStable:false, never propagating); for each manager enumerateManagers finds, calls verifyManagerClosureCoverage before (gating whether it is audited at all, 'unsupported' if not covered) and after (a post-audit regression also sets contentStable:false) its audit; invokes pkgAuditTool per manager with the t5-generated requirementsPath + noDeps:true for pipenv/poetry, or the project's own requirements.txt with no noDeps for plain pip; maps each manager's raw output into SecurityAdvisoryMatch[]; records every manager's configuredDestination and perManagerMode, and accounts every queried coordinate into exactly one of matches/unresolvedDependencies/queriedCoordinates-only.
acceptanceChecks: a manager's closure is covered:true pre-audit but covered:false post-audit (a new file appeared during the audit) -> contentStable:false, that manager's own results are still returned
a targets.entries file deleted between the pre- and post-collection computeContentIdentity calls -> contentStable:false, no exception escapes collectDependencyAdvisories
the FIRST computeContentIdentity call's own repoPath-level precondition failure DOES propagate (distinct from the second-call case)
a generated requirementsPath (pipenv/poetry) is ALWAYS invoked with noDeps:true; plain pip's own requirements.txt is NEVER invoked with noDeps:true
pkg_audit spawnError for a manager -> recorded in unavailableSources, never thrown
every attempted manager's perManagerMode entry carries a configuredDestination

a cleanly-checked coordinate with no advisory match appears in queriedCoordinates only; a coordinate with a confirmed finding appears in matches; an unresolved/unavailable coordinate appears in unresolvedDependencies/unavailableSources -- never more than one of these three
